subject: Bullying Prevention and Intervention Plan Policy Approval
overview: The School Committee deliberated on and approved a revised Bullying Prevention and Intervention Plan Policy, focusing on the definition of bullying, caregiver notification, and language accessibility. The body adopted several amendments to ensure parents receive incident reports and have access to translation services during investigations.

items.title: Rule 46 Suspension
items.summary: Approved the suspension of Rule 46 to allow for the adoption of the bullying policy upon its first reading.

items.title: Bullying Definition and Power Differential
items.summary: Discussed whether to include a 'power differential' in the definition of bullying to distinguish it from conflict. A motion to remove the power differential language failed, but a later compromise was approved to state that a finding of bullying is pursuant to the state definition and 'may' occur when students are not equal in power.

items.title: Translation and Interpretation Services
items.summary: Approved an amendment to provide interpretation and translation services for families to ensure comprehensive collaboration during the bullying intervention process.

items.title: Caregiver Incident Reporting
items.summary: Approved an amendment requiring that caregivers receive redacted incident reports resulting from bullying investigations promptly. The committee also noted that the policy will be updated once a broader incident reporting policy is codified in the fall.

items.title: Record Keeping and Civil Rights Information
items.summary: Approved amendments to include Office of Civil Rights contact information in the policy and to specify that bullying reports are placed in student records as required by law.

items.title: Approval of Policy JICFB
items.summary: Approved the Medford Public Schools Bullying Prevention and Intervention Plan Policy (JICFB) as amended.

items.title: Executive Session
items.summary: Referred items to executive session to discuss strategy for negotiations with Teamsters Local 25, review non-unit administrator contracts, and discuss security personnel deployment.
